newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open lower Tuesday in line with LME copper prices after a further rise in LME warehouse copper stocks.
COMEX September was called down 0.5 to 1.0 cent from Monday's close of 105.20 cents a lb after trading from 105.60 to 104.10 on ACCESS.
LME warehouse copper stocks rose a further 3,900 tonnes in Tuesday's data to 254,300 tonnes, the highest level since September 1996.
COMEX copper stocks rose 416 short tons Monday to 33,292 short tons.
The seasonal lull in demand and lower Chinese demand for copper in the first half of the year than in 1996 is seen behind the rise stocks.
The LME cash-to-three month spread has narrowed to around $18.00 a tonne this week, from over $240 a tonnein early July reflecting the easier prompt market conditions.
Copper prices have been consolidating in the past few weeks after a slide from 12-month highs a month ago.
